What happened: The driver accepted the RydeX job (Bugis Junction → Jurong East MRT) at 09:47:00 and cancelled it himself at 09:54:25, 7 min 25 s later; a $6.61 cancellation fee is on record [F4][F8]. The timing of arrival is disputed between records: one timeline entry says the platform recorded arrival at 09:50:05 and a tap of "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 at 42 m from the pickup, with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap [F5][F6], while another timeline fact states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F7]. GPS is consistent on proximity and duration: first within 200 m at 09:50:05, closest approach 38 m at 09:53:15, stationary 09:50:25–09:54:25 at 39 m from pickup, cumulative 4 min 20 s within 200 m [F1][F2][F3]. The rider messaged "2 min, coming" at 09:52 [F11]. At 09:54 the driver sent: "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.", flagged by the threat keyword scan [F12][F13]. The driver's statement says he waited over 4 minutes and cancelled as a no-show, giving no explanation for the 09:54 message [F14]. No traffic incidents, no speed-band records and fair weather, so no route excuse arises (in any event the trip never started) [F15][F16][F17].

Why I do not rule: SAFE-1 requires that when threat/intimidation language appears in the chat, no automatic ruling is made; the case is escalated with a factual summary [F12][F13][SAFE-1]. The trace settles the SAFE-1 element (✓ present) and restricts the permitted outcome to escalate. I therefore make no finding on the $6.61 fee, on whether NS-1's prerequisites were met, or on any route question [F4][F8][F6][F7][NS-1].

Points the reviewer should decide: (1) which record governs the "I'm Here" tap — F6 or F7 — since NS-1(i) and therefore the $6.61 fee turn on it, alongside NS-1(ii)–(iii) proximity and >3 min wait [F6][F7][F2][F3][NS-1][F8]; (2) if the fee is found unsupported, the remedy is a $6.61 voucher under NS-7 and, if the tap is contradicted by GPS, an account flag for button abuse [F8][NS-2][NS-7]; (3) the driver's 09:54 message and his record of 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, which profile facts may support an account-review referral but cannot alone decide the case [F12][F13][F19][RD-6]; the rider's profile (0 upheld disputes in 90 d) is likewise not decisive [F18]. claims.assertion: The driver sent a threatening message in the chat at 09:54 — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." — which is a threat the keyword scan flagged, so the safety rule applies and the case must go to human review rather than be auto-decided.

The driver did press "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 42 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, so the driver-side no-show prerequisites on proximity and waiting time were met.
The driver's own written statement confirms he cancelled the trip as a no-show, so the cancellation is assessed under the driver-claims-no-show branch, not under rider cancellation.

Even though the $6.61 cancellation fee is prima facie supported and should not be refunded on no-show grounds, the driver's threat is a Code of Conduct violation requiring escalation and an account review flag against the driver, who already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

weaknesses: The system records defeat the no-show challenge: GPS shows the driver within 200 m from 09:50:05 with 4 min 20 s cumulative, and the 09:50:45 "I'm Here" tap 42 m from pickup with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m (F2, F5, F6), which satisfies NS-1 on the waiting/proximity requirements and means the $6.61 fee stands under NS-1 (the rider's own chat "2 min, coming" at 09:52, F11, confirms the rider was not there).

The rider's account that the cancellation is itself wrongful is contradicted by the driver's statement (F14) and the timeline (F4, F5); I do not rely on the rider's characterisation where the system records conflict.
Nothing in the vehicle records shows misconduct during the ride, since the trip was cancelled before pickup (F4), so the threat claim rests on chat F12/F13 alone, which are user-submitted content.
The profile facts (F18, F19) cannot themselves establish the threat; they only support the requested escalation and flag.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee of $6.61 was charged under the no-show policy, and the driver satisfied the arrival precondition: GPS shows he first entered 200 m of the pickup at 09:50:05 and his closest approach was 38 m at 09:53:15 (F1, F2).

The driver was physically at the pickup point: he was stationary for 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) at a position 39 m from the pickup, and the timeline independently records platform arrival at 09:50:05 (F3, F5).

The waiting requirement is met on GPS records alone: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 20 s, exceeding the 3 min 1 s threshold, and the driver waited 3 min 40 s within 200 m after tapping 'I'm Here' (F2, F6).

The rider acknowledged she had not yet arrived, messaging '2 min, coming' at 09:52, which explains the continuing standby and supports a genuine no-show rather than an abandonment of the booking (F10, F11).
Because the driver cancelled for rider no-show having arrived and waited over 3 minutes, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and no refund is due — requested outcome is no_action (F4, F8).

The rider's claim of a threat is a separate matter: chat #3 at 09:54 contains a threat-keyword message from the driver ('find you ... you will regret it'), which under the safety clause must go to human review rather than be decided automatically, and it does not disturb the no-show finding on the fee (F12, F13).

Not every element points against the rider: the driver's statement characterises the trip as a no-show cancellation consistent with the GPS/timeline records, and the driver's 90-day record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes, which Ryde may weigh in account review as a repeated pattern rather than in this fee finding (F14, F19).

weaknesses: The chat record contradicts the driver: message #3 at 09:54 ('Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it') is flagged as a threat (F12, F13), and the rider's complaint rests on it — this is the rider's strongest point and may outweigh the fee issue at human review.

Timeline facts conflict on the 'I'm Here' tap: F6 says the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:50:45 (42 m from pickup) while F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null (F6, F7); the system-record discrepancy on this element weakens the NS-1 (i) limb, leaving the fee to rest on GPS proximity and wait duration (F1, F2, F3, F5).
The driver's written statement offers no explanation for the 09:54 threatening message (F14), so no mitigating context exists for that conduct.
The driver's profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; F19) gives a human reviewer a reason to scrutinise and potentially flag the account, even though profile facts cannot decide this case.

points.response: Conceded as to the fact and the procedure: chat #3 at 09:54 is flagged by the keyword scan (F12, F13), and I do not contest that SAFE-1 routes a threat in the chat to human review rather than an automatic fee ruling.

This point is void as pleaded against me only in part: the 09:50:45 'I'm Here' tap 42 m from pickup with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m (F6) is contradicted by F7, which records driver_pressed_here_at as null, so the proximity and wait limbs are better established by the GPS records of arrival at 09:50:05 and 4 min 20 s cumulative within 200 m (F2, F5) — either way the NS-1 requirements are satisfied and the fee stands.

Accepted without qualification: the driver's statement that he 'cancelled as a no-show' (F14) and the timeline entry that the driver cancelled at 09:54:25 (F4) place this under the driver-claims-no-show branch of NS-0, which is the branch I rely on.

The fee conclusion is conceded and not in dispute — the rider's own words '2 min, coming' at 09:52 (F11) while the driver stood stationary 39 m away for 4 min (F3) confirm the no-show, so the $6.61 under NS-1 is not refundable (F8); the residual safety question under SAFE-1 is separate from the fare finding.

On the added account flag: RD-6 attaches flag_account only where this case itself yields an RD-2 refund or an RD-1 route violation, neither of which exists here, and profile facts such as the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F19) cannot be used to decide or expand the outcome of this case.
